title: Track Apple silicon memory integration: CPU/GPU closeout, Core ML, and working-set optimization
body:
## Purpose

Track Apple silicon data and memory integration without losing follow-up research. The supported foundation carries data through ingestion, selection, preprocessing, computation, and result access with explicit numerical and ownership contracts. Resource efficiency includes CPU work, retained and peak memory, conversion, synchronization, and completed workflow costs.

This is a development tracker on our fork. It does not establish upstream commitments or maintainer approval. Follow-on experiments keep the tracker open after individual production milestones close.

## Current status, October 26, 2026

[CSV closeout #87](https://github.com/Nodibell/SwiftSci/pull/87) and [foundation closeout #88](https://github.com/Nodibell/SwiftSci/pull/88) are merged upstream. [Prepared PCA #89](https://github.com/Nodibell/SwiftSci/pull/89) remains open at `4f33c76f3938e070105c2a5928c712aa5e067a00`; its observed main, benchmark and CodeQL workflows passed. The maintainer-requested dimension/workspace corrections are included. This does not imply approval or merging of later fork branches.

The fork's combined scientific/inference source `c4de6cc866fff6f52100535dbcb38dd708558200` joins that complete PCA stack with prepared classification, the GPU gradient correction and the later Core ML work. It also replaces the documentation checker's false 100% claim with measured heuristic reporting. Native Debug and Release each pass 1,696 tests; local main/benchmark workflows, Swift 6.3.3 compatibility and Python CodeQL pass. [Integration records](https://github.com/crabel99/SwiftSci/blob/codex/engineering-notes/Documentation/EngineeringNotes/benchmarks/2026-10-26-scientific-ai-integration/README.md).

The next qualified fork source, `0e1635199654ac6a20b32ea53eea0ffdfa39e747` on `codex/llm-completion-contract`, preserves detailed model completion metadata before agent parsing/tool execution and fixes cooperative consumer cancellation in a separate commit. Legacy text-only models remain compatible; their completion status stays unknown. Cancellation cannot force arbitrary work to stop or undo side effects. Native Debug and Release each pass 1,712 tests, local main/benchmark workflows pass, and Swift 6.3.3 compatibility passes. Python CodeQL reports zero findings; matching-compiler Swift CodeQL completes with one unchanged legacy PostgreSQL MD5 finding, preserved as open authentication-policy debt. Xcode 27 remains selected. [Agent records](https://github.com/crabel99/SwiftSci/blob/codex/engineering-notes/Documentation/EngineeringNotes/benchmarks/2026-10-26-agent-completion-cancellation/README.md).

A [copyable complete numerical template](https://github.com/crabel99/SwiftSci/blob/codex/engineering-notes/Documentation/EngineeringNotes/benchmarks/2026-10-26-numerical-template/template/README.md) uses existing public APIs for training-only imputation/scaling, prepared PCA, prepared logistic classification and row-aligned held-out predictions. Independent scalar calculations agree within the declared 1e-12 absolute/relative check; the legacy path agrees exactly. Its pinned remote package was fetched, built and run successfully, with complete output equality to the independently verified workflow. This toy example establishes integration, not predictive quality, performance or a memory bound.

[Representative weighted ML Program records](https://github.com/crabel99/SwiftSci/blob/codex/engineering-notes/Documentation/EngineeringNotes/benchmarks/2026-10-26-mlprogram-representative/README.md) preserve frozen real-data models, 52 bounded stress cases and complete output comparisons. Reduced internal precision exceeds the unchanged strict Double check, `abs(error) <= 1e-5 + 1e-5 * abs(reference)`; full-Float32 compute controls meet it. Float32 I/O alone does not imply Float32 computation. Actual inspected events establish CPU dispatch, not Neural Engine acceleration. The earlier [legacy Core ML study](https://github.com/crabel99/SwiftSci/blob/codex/engineering-notes/Documentation/EngineeringNotes/benchmarks/2026-10-26-coreml-representative/README.md) remains separately fingerprinted.

Across the current benchmark policy's 404 executions, 400 pass strict conformance and four reviewed Python Wampler failures remain failed. The policy passes without weakening tolerances or changing the failure inventory. These are local qualifications on one Mac, separate from hosted checks and upstream delivery.

The [engineering-record index](https://github.com/crabel99/SwiftSci/blob/codex/engineering-notes/Documentation/EngineeringNotes/README.md) links the dated evidence. Historical records below retain their tested revisions and conclusions.

## Measurement boundary and next actions

- [x] Finish bounded foundation audits and correct the demonstrated native copy, schema, and capacity-accounting gaps.
- [x] Validate both delivery heads independently and preserve the completed E-core resource study.
- [x] Publish the supported data and memory contract and both draft review units.
- [x] Complete hosted checks and upstream delivery for #87 and #88.
- [ ] Complete upstream review/delivery of #89; keep the separately qualified scientific/inference and agent fork branches distinct until their delivery scope is reviewed.
- [x] Qualify representative weighted Core ML workflows, ownership/provenance and reduced- versus full-compute precision; preserve observed CPU placement and strict precision failures.
- [x] Provide one runnable public numerical workflow template and verify its stage outputs independently.
- [ ] Decide the legacy PostgreSQL MD5 authentication policy and validate SCRAM migration separately; retain the existing Swift CodeQL finding.
- [ ] Establish a repeatable timing baseline. The full E-core panel retains ten CPU or elapsed-time twin failures and one 0.526 ms observation overrun. Memory controls pass; compact storage uses about 28.4% less sampled peak memory than optional storage in both conditions. Timing results remain unqualified, and the exact Apple operating-state mechanism is unproven.

Follow-on research is separate from this phase-one contract: broader representative inference and placement evidence, cache and working-set counters, shared-bandwidth contention, false-sharing experiments, custom Metal staging, general mutable foreign buffers, and automatic hardware routing. The optional second identity-provenance preparation copy is already allowance-covered and remains a minor follow-up, not an unresolved lifetime failure.

## Retained milestone checklist

The checklist below preserves prior milestones and research tasks. Completed CPU/GPU entries describe the earlier delivered contributions; the new closeout PR delivery remains tracked above.

## 1. Close the current CPU/GPU contribution

- [x] Inventory production changes, experimental owners and benchmark-only paths against the intended contribution base. Identify what ships and what remains research.
- [x] Resolve the supported ownership boundary for `RetainedLinearRegressionTrial`, `RetainedGPUInputTrial`, and `RetainedPreparedGPUInputTrial`. Promotion requires caller and lifetime review, not just renaming.
- [x] Reconcile dependency and upstream changes; preserve existing public behavior, numerical policies, source snapshots and compatibility entry points.
- [x] Document supported dtypes, layouts, missing-value semantics, cancellation/completion behavior, and the limits of estimated admission budgets.
- [x] Run the applicable Debug/Release, numerical-policy, documentation and lifecycle checks on the final contribution revision. Keep skipped or unverified cases explicit.
- [x] Preserve benchmark fingerprints, rerun comparisons affected by consolidation, and record the reviewed local contribution and evidence.

Exit condition: a bounded, reviewable CPU/GPU contribution with an explicit supported contract and validation at its final head. Later accelerator experiments do not block this milestone.

Local closeout completed October 7, 2026 on `codex/cpu-gpu-optimization-closeout` at `22c6b8908b18c967295f08a5effa69265c7fa4ef`; implementation commit `e29002e7d0`. It is based on PR #62 and includes the merged #60 dependency update with no change to the tested tree. The trial head remains preserved. Retained-owner APIs and comparison controls stay experimental; in particular, the retained prediction adapter needs an explicit GPU/precision contract before promotion.

Validation: 1,208 Debug and 1,208 Release tests passed, with two optional skips in each configuration; 160 controller tests and 100 workflow validation controls passed. All 196 Swift numerical cases passed; the Python reference retains four reviewed Wampler failures out of 196 cases. Regression policy passed without changing tolerances. Across 48 comparison workers and 299,520 requests, predictions and fitted parameters matched; lifecycle checks passed. Median throughput changes against the preserved trial ranged from -1.44% to +1.03%, a bounded qualification rather than a statistical equivalence claim. Eight additional integrity workers checked retained-source preservation and consumed-buffer reuse.

Evidence is recorded locally on `codex/engineering-notes` at `5ce0758617b4a172b1aaed882f19d82c0e4048ff`, in `Documentation/EngineeringNotes/benchmarks/2026-10-07-cpu-gpu-closeout.md`. Neither new branch head has been pushed. Runtime qualification is on the current Apple silicon host, not every supported macOS version.

- [x] Publish the reviewed CPU/GPU contribution with its dependency on #62 clear, link its PR and published evidence, and complete hosted CI. Publication is separate from the completed local development/qualification above.

## 2. Add a Core ML execution interface on a separate branch

- [x] Audit and reuse existing `CoreMLExportable` / `CoreMLExporter` support and relevant Apple APIs before introducing new abstractions.
- [x] Connect prepared data to Core ML inputs and outputs with explicit dtype, shape, stride, conversion, and ownership contracts. Evaluate compatible shared backing and reusable output buffers; verify copies rather than assuming their absence.
- [x] Keep application admission and buffer lifetimes in our memory layer. Leave model partitioning, Neural Engine scheduling and internal memory placement with Core ML.
- [x] Expose allowed compute units and fallback behavior honestly. An allowed Neural Engine does not prove execution there.
- [x] Qualify asynchronous prediction, cancellation, errors, concurrent requests, model unload and repeated reuse. Account separately for application estimates and observed framework/process memory.
- [x] Use frozen representative supported inference models and independently check complete outputs across legacy Core ML and weighted ML Programs. Preserve reduced-precision failures and successful full-Float32 compute controls.
- [x] Inspect actual runtime placement for the tested weighted ML Programs. Record CPU dispatch and the absence of established Neural Engine acceleration; allowed compute units are not placement proof.
- [ ] Extend representative CPU/GPU/Neural Engine placement and performance comparisons where available, including conversion, cold/warm latency, throughput, memory and application accuracy. Existing results do not complete this broader item.

Status: the first verified workflow is delivered by #65 and #66, with end-to-end bounding in #67. Broader device-placement and compute-policy comparisons remain ongoing; allowed compute units do not establish actual placement.

Exit condition: one complete, verified workflow through the adapter, with documented fallback and ownership behavior. General dataframe operations and FP64 scientific computation do not become implicit NPU workloads.

## 3. Measure and optimize working sets

Each item starts as a hypothesis with a reference implementation. Retain an optimization only when representative measurements support its tradeoff.

- [ ] Characterize actively reused bytes, dtype, access order, strides and concurrency across realistic sizes. Separate software overhead, allocation, conversion, computation and synchronization. Use hardware counters where available and distinguish observations from inferred cache effects.
- [x] Evaluate compact columns and validity storage through ingestion and numerical consumers. Include selection, missing values, retained snapshots, mutations and conversion costs.
- [x] Evaluate blocked matrix operations and packing with varied shapes and reuse counts. Compare established Accelerate/BLAS paths before adding custom kernels; avoid a universal hard-coded crossover from one fixture or chip.
- [x] Evaluate fusion of compatible preprocessing steps over chunks to reduce intermediate arrays and memory passes. Preserve training-only fitting, arithmetic/precision requirements, missing-value treatment and source ownership.
- [ ] Evaluate worker partitioning, task size and concurrent writes for false sharing and bandwidth contention. Measure whether padding or partition changes justify their extra memory cost.
- [ ] Compare Metal threadgroup staging with direct access for a suitable workload. Include occupancy, synchronization and staging costs; do not assume explicit scratch memory is faster.
- [ ] Test CPU/GPU/Core ML handoffs and overlapping work for shared-bandwidth contention, completion ordering and memory pressure. Unified addressing does not make accesses equally cheap or remove synchronization.

Exit condition per experiment: an adopted change with evidence, or a documented rejection/deferment explaining when to reconsider it. This milestone does not promise that every proposed optimization will ship.

## 4. Keep the roadmap and evidence usable

- [ ] Record each experiment's hypothesis, branch, baseline/candidate commits, workloads, numerical contract, result and decision in the engineering notes; link it here once published.
- [ ] Use child issues for substantial work, each with an acceptance condition and a bounded branch/PR. Reference this tracker in those issues and PRs without automatically closing it.
- [ ] Maintain a representative comparison across small/large/mixed inputs, retained/consumed ownership, cold/warm execution and bounded concurrency. Include end-to-end costs and relevant Python/framework references with equivalent contracts.
- [ ] Record supported-hardware and OS coverage, unavailable counters, untested failure paths, and performance regressions. Preserve historical results at their tested fingerprints.
- [x] Update this issue's completed work, next action and deferred items at the October 26 milestone. Continue doing so for future milestones.

## Reference material

- [Apple CPU performance and false-sharing guidance](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/tech-talks/110147/)
- [Apple Metal shader guidance](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/tech-talks/111373/)
- [Metal shared storage](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/mtlstoragemode/shared)
- [Apple Neural Engine transformer layout and memory guidance](https://machinelearning.apple.com/research/neural-engine-transformers), a documented implementation study rather than a universal layout rule for every chip generation.
- [Core ML input/output and performance integration](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2022/10027/)

The October 26 status above is the current checkpoint. Earlier milestone sections retain historical source fingerprints and results. Broader cache counters, false sharing, Metal staging, shared-bandwidth contention and automatic routing remain research tasks, not promised production additions.
